new:
- ONE psGrades TEXT FOR EVERY CALLER (ASK 474; Shared Library only, engine and child):
    - Why: psGrades stood in the library as three source texts: A (13 gate, late gate and merge stubs), B (Send Back Record, Alt Send Back Record, R2 Alt Send Back Record) and C (Cure Check, Panel Cure Check; A plus one comment). B lacked the ri3Head2024 head reader (pkgRI3B) and the rule that a quotation ending a sentence keeps the sentence break (pkgPSQ), so a fix to A did not reach the send-back records.
    - What it does: B and C are removed and their five stubs rebuild from A; the three Send Back stubs also gain ri3Head2024. The send-back records now read a CONCEDED LINKS line the way the gates read it. Library lines 3503 to 3499; the second psGrades definition and its split line are gone, so earlier entries that name two psGrades copies now mean the one. The ASK 385 registry no longer accepts two psGrades texts.
    - Shown offline: every other stub rebuilds byte for byte; no comment text added; noderep on 5 stored executions shows no node output change; old B against new A on 1,360 stored CONCEDED LINKS lines: 22 parsed by both, 0 readings changed.
    - Live: engine 5c0f00ab and child b10fcad2 (from 839d34ad and a5b4e84b), library 56c66d536f088f5d on both (was 40d3eb4e7d3bc276), on the operator's card "Write it" pressed 14:10:27Z on 11-19.
    - Limits: not shown by a run; only 22 stored lines exercise the B reader, so the new B behavior is shown equal on stored data, not on a head the old B missed. Its mark is a run with a send-back whose sb_rows match what the gate nodes read for the same lines.
